recap.text: Stairwells join floors and halve in number as crawlers descend. Anyone who descends early is held in stasis until the collapse. A pink, fleshy creature stinking of sewage guards a stairwell at the heart of a round maze. A level-93 rage elemental dissolves in a stairwell hole, but the dungeon patches the rule so non-sapient mobs no longer disintegrate.

The circus tents and corpses vanish from the park, leaving a staircase down to the fourth floor. Mordecai says stairwells often become visible after a quest. Another stairwell sits three kilometres east of the settlement in a decrepit building. Crawlers leave notes in bars with stairwell locations. A door at the bottom reads Entrance to the fourth floor. This is where the real fun begins. Mind the gap.

Milk writes in the Cookbook that a stairwell cannot go into a saferoom or an inventory, and one survived a hit by an Utter Annihilation wand. The rules manual states stairwells may be gated but never removed. In Turkey, former Daughters kill a crawler for his key and damage the door, causing the key to disappear. They dig down to find a sealed rectangular room like a shipping container where a Hole spell and Phase Through Walls do nothing.

beats.headline: The way down is lit from below
beats.text: Every floor is joined to the next by many of them, halving in number each floor down, and a crawler must find one and descend before that floor's time runs out. They are generally well lit, and the warmth comes up rather than down, so a crawler standing at the top is being invited by something that has already decided what happens next.
beats.gist: Stairwells join floors and halve in number each floor down before time runs out.

beats.headline: Don't go down early
beats.text: After the premiere the staircases down to the next level begin to populate, with a warning attached. Once down, a crawler cannot come back up, and this season anyone who descends early is held in stasis until the collapse, out of sight while viewers lose interest and favorites drain away. The recommendation is to go down no earlier than six hours before the floor collapses; inside that window there is no stasis, and a head start over everyone already frozen at the bottom.
beats.gist: Staircases populate after the premiere with a warning that crawlers who descend early face stasis.

beats.headline: At the centre of a spiral
beats.text: The first stairwell down after a day's drive sits at the heart of a great round maze, and something rolls around its rings fast enough to shake the walls: pink, fleshy, as tall as the hallway, stinking of sewage. Mordecai had said the bosses would not guard stairwells until the fourth floor. The graffiti left by whoever got here first says otherwise: this road is safe, do not go deeper, or you activate the borough boss.
beats.gist: The first stairwell sits in a round maze where a pink, sewage-stinking creature shakes the walls.

beats.headline: Mobs do not go down
beats.text: A goblin shamanka told them once: mobs that climb down the stairs dissolve halfway. The guide said the same. So a level-93 rage elemental, which nobody here can kill, is lured across an oil slick into a stairwell hole, and the dungeon follows its own rules. The elemental dissolves with its health already in the red and a bomb going off beside it. Nobody is credited with the kill, and nobody gets the experience.
beats.gist: A level-93 rage elemental dissolves in a stairwell hole after crossing an oil slick.

beats.headline: The stairwell rule is patched
beats.text: The exploit gets its own paragraph in the next announcement. Yes, everyone just watched that rule get exploited on the recap. It was very clever and very exciting. It is not going to happen again. Effective immediately, any non-sapient mob that happens upon a stairwell will not be disintegrated. The same message says game guides may now explain the third floor's race and class selection.
beats.gist: The stairwell rule is patched so non-sapient mobs are not disintegrated and guides explain race and class.

beats.headline: Under the circus
beats.text: By morning the circus tents are gone, and so are the corpses and whatever a city boss might have dropped. In their place, in the middle of the park, is a staircase down to the fourth floor. It never showed on the map before, not even as one they could not reach, the way the Ball of Swine's did. Mordecai says many stairwells from here down only become visible once a quest is completed. This one had probably been sitting under Grimaldi the whole time.
beats.gist: A staircase to the fourth floor appears in the park after the circus tents and corpses vanish.

beats.headline: Mind the gap
beats.text: This one sits three kilometres east of the settlement in a small, decrepit building, and with the saferooms shut and the Desperado Club's back room sealed, it is the only way out of the blast. Crawlers have been leaving notes in the bars with stairwell locations. A floor ends for whoever goes down the moment they pull the handle at the bottom. The door there carries the usual oversized carving, and its properties read: Entrance to the fourth floor. This is where the real fun begins. Mind the gap.
beats.gist: A stairwell in a decrepit building provides the only way out of the blast.

beats.headline: The stairs hold; the doors do not
beats.text: A note from Milk in the Cookbook says a stairwell cannot go into an inventory or a saferoom, and one hit by an Utter Annihilation wand came through unscathed. The rules manual agrees: stairwells may be gated, never removed. The doors are another matter. A team of former Daughters in Turkey kill a crawler for his key, damage the door in the fight, and watch the key disappear. They dig down and find the chamber: a sealed rectangular room like a shipping container, with a straight wall where the door was. A Hole spell does nothing. Neither does Phase Through Walls.
beats.gist: A note from Milk and the rules manual state stairwells cannot be removed.
